Hæc namjue caligo, est æternæ, increatæ, infinitæque lucis divine superexcellens, incomprehensibilis et superclarissima plenitudo, abyssalis, interminabilis atque supersimplicissima magnitudo, in qua Deus esse et habitare censetur, qui ponit tenebras (id est infinitam hanc lucem, omnem creatarum mentium capacitatem infinite transcendentem ac superantem) latibulum suum ; et ipsæ divinæ tenebræ cooperiuntur et absconduntur omni visioni ac lumini, ob incircumscriptibilem suam plenitudinem, prorsus impenetrabilem et immensam. Quum itaque mens æstuantissimo caritatis ardore succensa, Deo ita conjungitur per contemplationem theoricam et sapientiam luminosam, flammigeram, unitivam, dicitur introire caliginem, instarque Moysis ab omnibus separari. Unitur enim Deo tanquam prorsus incomprehensibili, et quoad quid est, mere ignoto: et tamen hoc ipsum sic intueri, est clarissime ac suavissime contemplari, speciesque altissima contemplationis huic vitæ possibilis. Ideireo tunc tota in lucem illam tam infinitam expanditur, increatæ veritati infigitur, superessentiali deitati et superbeatissimæ Trinitati tam radiose, amorose et proxime copulatur, quod aliud nihil advertit, nec proprium actum attendit, sed defluit a se ipsa, atque in proprium refluit fontem. Sicque in divitias gloriæ rapitur, in amoris increati immensi igne comburitur, in deitatis abyssum profundatur et absorbetur, ut videatur quodammodo esse creatum exuere, et increatum idealeque esse induere : non quod substantia mutetur aut proprium esse tollatur, sed quoniam modus essendi, qualitasque vivendi deificatur, hoc est, Deo et superbeatissimæ beatitudini ejus supernaturaliter et gratiosissime assimilatur, sicque eminenter impletur illud Apostoli : Qui adhæret Domino, unus spiritus est; imo quod in Joanne loquitur Unitas ipsa et Veritas increata Unigenitus Patris : Pater, rogo pro eis qui credituri sunt in me, ut omnes unum sint, sicut tu, Pater, in me, et ego in te, ut et ipsi in nobis unum sint. Ego in eis et tu in me, ut sint consummati in unum ; ut dilectio qua dilexisti me, in ipsis sit, et ego in ipsis.
paras.en: [[20:21|And the people stood afar off. But Moses went to the dark cloud wherein God was.|Stetitque populus de longe. Moyses autem accessit ad caliginem in qua erat Deus.]] This clause the great and most theological Dionysius interprets most profoundly in his book On Mystical Theology, understanding by Moses any heroic and perfect man who, having left behind and passed beyond all things of sense and of intellect, indeed all created things, and himself and all his own acts, is united to God by most ardent love, and enters the darkness [caligo, the 'dark cloud' of the verse] in which God truly is. For this darkness is the surpassing, incomprehensible and more-than-radiant fullness of the eternal, uncreated and infinite divine light, an abyssal, boundless and utterly simple greatness, in which God is held to be and to dwell, who [[Ps 17:12|made darkness his cover|posuit tenebras latibulum suum]] (that is, this infinite light, which infinitely transcends and surpasses every capacity of created minds); and this divine darkness is covered and hidden from all sight and all light by its uncircumscribable fullness, wholly impenetrable and immeasurable. So when the mind, set on fire with the most burning ardour of charity, is thus joined to God by contemplative vision and by wisdom that is luminous, fiery and unitive, it is said to enter the darkness and, like Moses, to be separated from all things. For it is united to God as to One wholly incomprehensible and, as to what He is, simply unknown; and yet so to behold this very thing is to contemplate most clearly and most sweetly, and is the highest kind of contemplation possible in this life. Therefore the whole mind is then spread out into that infinite light, fixed on the uncreated truth, and joined to the superessential Godhead and the most blessed Trinity so radiantly, so lovingly and so closely, that it notices nothing else and does not attend to its own act, but flows away from itself and flows back into its own source. And so it is caught up into the riches of glory, burned in the fire of uncreated, immense love, plunged and swallowed up in the abyss of the Godhead, so that it seems in some way to put off its created being and to put on uncreated, ideal being: not that its substance is changed or its own being taken away, but because its mode of being and its manner of life are deified, that is, made like to God and to His most blessed beatitude, supernaturally and most graciously. And so that saying of the Apostle is fulfilled in an eminent way: [[1 Cor 6:17|he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit|Qui autem adhæret Domino, unus spiritus est]]; indeed, so is what the very Unity and uncreated Truth, the Only-begotten of the Father, says in John: Father, I pray for them [[John 17:20|who through their word shall believe in me|qui credituri sunt per verbum eorum in me]]: [[John 17:21|That they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee; that they also may be one in us|ut omnes unum sint, sicut tu Pater in me, et ego in te, ut et ipsi in nobis unum sint]].
